decision.core_belief: Zoetis owns the strongest franchise in animal health — 70% gross margins, pricing power across pets and livestock, and a pipeline that just added a next-generation 75-day itch-relief antibody in Cytopoint Plus. The business is under real pressure right now from generic competition in dermatology, softer vet visit volumes, and a companion animal market that is repricing in a cost-conscious consumer environment, but those are cyclical and competitive headwinds, not franchise destruction. What has to stay true: gross margins hold at or above 70%, the livestock and diagnostics segments keep growing to offset companion animal softness, and new products like Cytopoint Plus extend pricing power in dermatology over time.

decision.rationale: HeartFlow reported Q3 2026 yesterday — revenue up 57% year-over-year to $72.9M, gross margin 83.6%, EPS beat of 71%, and full-year guidance raised. The stock was up to $60+ intraday but closed today at $49.31, down 17.7%, likely on profit-taking after the run. Three sell-side analysts raised their price targets this morning — Canaccord to $69, Stifel to $70, Baird to $68 — well above the stale consensus average of $48.50. The prior PASS from August was based on a weaker setup; the business has since delivered a second consecutive strong beat, revenue growth has accelerated materially, and the street is now revising upward. The stock's pullback today puts it near the 50-day moving average at $51.94, which is the natural re-entry level if the uptrend holds.
decision.conviction_rationale: The business quality is real — 57% revenue growth, 83%+ gross margins, and two consecutive big beats — but the stock is loss-making, the street consensus target of $48.50 is below today's price, and I want to see the gap-day selling stabilize before committing. The three fresh targets of $68–$70 suggest the stale average will reprice upward quickly, which is a tailwind, but I'm sizing to a confirmed pullback hold rather than a full position.
decision.core_belief: HeartFlow makes AI-powered software that simulates blood flow in coronary arteries from a CT scan, letting cardiologists diagnose heart disease without invasive procedures. It earns revenue each time the analysis is run, so growth comes from hospitals and health systems adopting the technology and running more cases — a volume-driven model with very high gross margins once the platform is in place. What has to stay true is that case volume keeps growing at a double-digit rate and gross margins hold above 80%, because those two things together are what turns the operating losses into eventual free cash flow.
decision.variant_view: Analysts have price targets averaging $48.50 — below today's price — because revisions haven't caught up to the Q3 beat yet. The three firms that raised targets this morning went to $68–$70, implying the consensus will re-rate significantly. I think the market is underpricing how durable 57% revenue growth is for a healthcare AI platform with 83% gross margins, and that the post-earnings selloff is institutional profit-taking rather than a signal about the business.
